title.narrative: Modern Skills for Better Jobs Sector Development Program, Subprogram 1

description.narrative: The Modern Skills for Better Jobs Sector Development Program will support the government's VET program to promote job creation in high-value sectors, economic growth, and reduce poverty. The proposed outputs are 1) Quality and relevance of vocational education and training improved, 2) Private participation in vocational education and training enhanced, and 3) Inclusiveness of vocational education and training system increased.The program outputs will result in the following outcome: a responsive VET network promoting excellence in skills development established. The program will be aligned with the following impact: potential of the country's human resources maximized.

description.narrative: Effect of the Reform: A responsive VET network promoting excellence in skills development strengthened

At least 65% of VET project skills hubs graduates in priority economic sectors, of whom at least 50% are women, are employed or self-employed 6 months after graduation. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet due
Labor market firm to carry out the tracer study of Skills Hubs' graduates, firm was contracted in November 2022. Data Source: Project administered tracer study.

At least 80% of employers express satisfaction with program graduates 6 months after graduation. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Not yet due
First batch of Skills Hubs' graduates are expected in 2026. Data Source: Project adminis-tered employer satisfaction survey.
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Quality and relevance of VET in priority economic sectors improved. Indicator: Two VET institutes upgraded to skills hubs, incorporating gender- and PWD-inclusive design features, in seven priority economic sectors. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Telavi hub is readvertised and tender was successful. The evaluation report will be submitted to ADB for approval. contract for Kutaisi hub is awarded Data Source: PIU reports

Output: Access to, and inclusiveness of, VET system increased Indicator: 20 project supported secondary schools providing gender-sensitive career guidance within new VET programs by Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The gender sensitive career guidance trainings were delivered in all target schools and skills hubs. Data Source: project reports

Output: Access to, and inclusiveness of, VET system increased Indicator: At least 2,000 people (1,100 female, 500 minorities, 200 special education needs) complete short-term VET Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: around 500 are already trained. Data Source: EMIS data

Output: Institutional framework strengthened through increased private participation in VET Indicator: At least 21 occupational standards developed or revised by SSOs with participation of employer representatives Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: 26 qualifications are approved Data Source: PIU reports

Output: Institutional framework strengthened through increased private participation in VET Indicator: At least 500 individuals (50% women) completed training in specialized internationally recognized programs Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Internationally accredited training provision is planned to be provided in Q4, 2025 through Q4 2026 by PIU PPP and Industry engagement Specialist. Data Source: PIU reports

Output: Institutional framework strengthened through increased private participation in VET Indicator: At least one public-private partnership for the private management of an institute or programs in place Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: The MOU on PPP in VET has been signed on December 2, 2024 between SA, Felder Group, TZ Austria and National Center of Woodworking traditions and technologies LtD. Data Source: Contract or similar agreement on outsourcing

Output: Quality and relevance of VET in priority economic sectors improved. Indicator: At least 5% of skills hubs' budget generated from non-MOESCS funds. Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: legislative changes to facilitate income generating activities in VET colleges (including Skills Hubs) have been submitted to the Parliament. Data Source: Skills hubs' financial reports

Output: Institutional framework strengthened through increased private participation in VET Indicator: Seven SSOs in priority sectors with 40% female members operational Achievement: 7 Progress/Status: 7 SSOs (Startup SSOs) have been established in ICT, Tourism, Artisan (furniture), Construction and Engineering, Energy, Healthcare and Personal Services (Medical and pharmaceutical production), Apparel and Fashion (Fashion and Design).
